title: EARN: Efficient Inference Acceleration for LLM-based Generative Recommendation by Register Tokens

problem.claim: LLM-based generative recommendation suffers from high inference latency due to computational overhead and KV Cache memory pressure.

gap.claim: Existing KV Cache reduction methods are limited because cache compression offers marginal acceleration for short recommendation decoding steps, while prompt compression may discard vital interaction history.

contributions.claim: The work analyzes attention patterns in LLM-based generative recommendation and identifies layer-wise attention sparsity inversion and dual attention sinks.
EARN compresses information into register tokens at input sequence boundaries using early layers and focuses subsequent layers on those tokens.
EARN is presented as an efficient inference framework for LLM-based generative recommendation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three datasets, two LLMRec methods, and two LLM architectures report up to 3.79x speedup and 80.8% KV Cache reduction, with better accuracy than a general finetuning approach.
The authors report practical deployment advantages for industrial scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM-based generative recommendation has high inference latency caused by computational overhead and KV Cache memory pressure.
Existing KV Cache reduction approaches face limitations related to short decoding steps and preservation of interaction history.
Attention analysis reveals layer-wise sparsity inversion and dual attention sinks.
EARN uses early layers to compress information into boundary register tokens and restricts later layers to those tokens.
Experiments report speedup, KV Cache reduction, and improved accuracy across multiple datasets, methods, and architectures.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports that early layers retain dense informative patterns while later layers exhibit high redundancy, alongside attention concentration at sequence boundaries.

interpretation.claim: Inference acceleration may be possible by preserving information selectively across layers and sequence positions.

application.claim: For similar sequential recommendation systems, investigate layer- and position-aware representations before applying generic cache compression.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported attention patterns or acceleration generalize beyond the evaluated datasets, methods, and architectures.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated datasets, LLMRec methods, LLM architectures, or general finetuning baseline.
The abstract does not describe the experimental protocol, latency measurement conditions, or accuracy metrics.
